alt: A comparison of the two title types. An argumentative essay aims to persuade, states its position at the start, raises the other side only to answer it and ends by strengthening its case. A discursive essay explores more than one side, settles its position at the end, gives the other side fair space and ends with a balanced judgement.
caption: An argument holds one view throughout; a discussion weighs the sides and judges at the end.

alt: Three titles from the guide. One ending اس کے حق میں دلائل دیجیے is argumentative, one ending بحث کیجیے is discursive, and کیا آپ اس بات سے متفق ہیں کہ ...؟ allows either, as long as the answer is clear by the end.
caption: The wording of the instruction, not the topic, tells you which essay to write.

alt: Part 2 is marked out of 25: content 10 marks (W1 to W3), structure 5 marks (W4) and language 10 marks (W5, W6), with the top-level descriptors for each. Conditional (اگر ... تو), concessive (اگرچہ ... پھر بھی) and relative (وہ لوگ جو ...) sentences show range in an argument.
caption: Language carries as many marks as content; structure rewards ordered, linked ideas.

alt: Five planning steps: decide your thesis (دعویٰ), choose three main points, give each point evidence, note one objection, and write the last sentence first. Below, a 300-400-word essay as five paragraphs of 60 to 80 words: introduction, three body paragraphs and a conclusion.
caption: Thesis, three evidenced points, one objection, and the ending decided before you start.

alt: Urdu connectives grouped by purpose: ordering (اوّل تو، دوسرے یہ کہ، آخر میں), adding (علاوہ ازیں، مزید برآں), conceding (یہ درست ہے کہ ... لیکن، اگرچہ ... پھر بھی), contrasting (اس کے برعکس، تاہم) and concluding (لہٰذا، نتیجتاً). Repeating علاوہ ازیں at every paragraph signals a list.
caption: Choose each connective for the relationship it shows between two ideas.

alt: The plan for the public-transport title: a thesis that public transport must be the priority, three reasons (less congestion and lost time, cleaner air, fairness for those who cannot afford a car), and an objection that buses are slow and unsafe, answered as a fault of the present system. The introduction opens with a scene and ends with the thesis.
caption: One thesis, three reasons, and one objection answered.

alt: The model paragraph broken into five moves: it states the objection fairly (یہ اعتراض کیا جاتا ہے کہ ...), concedes in part (یہ شکایت بے بنیاد نہیں), turns it as a fault of the present system, uses a conditional sentence (جب ... تو), and returns to the thesis with گویا.
caption: State, concede, turn, then bring the paragraph back to your thesis.

after: ## Turning the same material into a discussion
alt: For the discursive title کیا ذاتی گاڑیوں پر پابندیاں لگانا درست ہوگا؟ بحث کیجیے, the single objection paragraph of the argument becomes a full side: families, people with no bus route and small traders. The conclusion then gives a judgement, such as limits only once a reliable alternative exists.
caption: In a discussion the other side gets real space, and the ending must still judge.
